title: CompTIA A+ Core 1 & Core 2 Foundations — The Four Rubber Bands

terms.title: RAM (Random Access Memory)
terms.definition: High-speed volatile semiconductor memory utilized by the processor to hold active program instructions, operating system kernel routines, and working data sets while powered.
terms.context: Loses all stored data instantly when electrical power is removed or interrupted during a reboot.
refs: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1101) Objective 3.1: Resolve problems with motherboard, RAM, CPU, and power

terms.title: Non-Volatile Storage
terms.definition: Secondary data persistence hardware such as solid-state drives, magnetic hard disks, or flash memory that retains stored binary data without continuous electrical power.
terms.context: Houses operating system installations, permanent application binaries, user documents, and system configuration registries across reboots.
refs: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1101) Objective 3.2: Troubleshoot storage drives and RAID arrays

terms.title: POST (Power-On Self-Test)
terms.definition: An initial diagnostic sequence executed by system firmware (BIOS or UEFI) immediately upon startup to verify and initialize core hardware components before loading the OS.
terms.context: Validates CPU registers, system memory integrity, display controllers, and bus interfaces, halting or emitting diagnostic beep/hex codes if essential hardware fails.
refs: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1101) Objective 3.1: Motherboard and boot sequence troubleshooting

terms.title: NIC (Network Interface Card)
terms.definition: A hardware expansion card or onboard controller that implements physical Layer 1 signaling and Layer 2 data link framing to connect a computer to a local network.
terms.context: Converts internal digital system bus transactions into serialized electrical, optical, or radio transmissions across physical network media.
refs: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1101) Objective 2.1: Compare and contrast network hardware devices

terms.title: MAC Address
terms.definition: A globally unique 48-bit physical identifier burned into the firmware of a network interface card by the manufacturer to facilitate Layer 2 frame delivery on local Ethernet segments.
terms.context: Operates exclusively within a single local broadcast domain, remaining unchanged across networks and never routing across internet boundaries.
refs: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1101) Objective 2.4: Summarize basic networking concepts

terms.title: IP Address
terms.definition: A logical 32-bit (IPv4) or 128-bit (IPv6) numerical identifier assigned to a network interface to enable routable packet delivery across interconnected Layer 3 network domains.
terms.context: Assigned dynamically via DHCP or statically by network administrators, reflecting the host's topological location on a logical subnet rather than its physical hardware identity.
refs: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1101) Objective 2.6: Configure basic networking host settings
